condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Output 1: Integrated governance to deliver on NDC outcomes Indicator 1: Number of improved institutionalised, governance, structures and processes for NDC implementation Results against targets attained under output 1 and indicator 1. Result for target 1.1: Final updated NDC for Uganda was approved by cabinet and submitted to United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in September 2022. In addition, the NDC implementation and resource mobilization plan has been developed to ensure effective implementation of the NDC.
Results for target 1.2: A National Post COP26 workshop was organised with key stakeholders including government Ministries, Departments and Agencies, CSOs, private sector and youth. The workshop discussed implications of the COP26 outcomes in the Ugandan context, how the outcomes will be implemented at national level, opportunities that COP26 presents for Uganda and discussed strategies that the country will undertake to implement the key outcomes and the roadmap to COP27
Result for target 1.3: Hosting for Uganda’s integrated MRV tool has been completed and the web hosting. Capacity development on the integrated MRV tool is expected to be conducted in December 2022.
Output 2: Capacities developed to design climate friendly investments, address investor risk, blend and catalyze climate finance. Indicator 2: Number of capacity development workshops held to design climate friendly investments Results against targets attained under output 2 and indicator 2 Results for for target 2.1: One workshop was held to discuss the draft NDC implementation plan. The stakeholder workshop was attended by 120 participants (70 M;50 F). The Draft NDC implementation and resource mobilization plan has been completed. A stakeholder consultation workshop was held to discuss the draft implementation plan. In addition, five project concept notes, describing 5 specific NDC measures have been prepared for resource mobilization.
The concept notes will be a starting point for resource mobilization for NDC implementation across different sectors. The five concept notes are developed under the following areas; - Sustainable multi-modal transport system in Uganda’s urban areas, including Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area (GKMA) through electric bus rapid transit, electric Standard Gauge Railway light rapid mass transit and non-motorized transport modes in the transport sector. - Restoring the health of agricultural Rangeland and Mountain Landscapes through Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) in Uganda’s Environment and Natural Resources Management; and Agriculture sectors. - De-risking the expansion of post-harvest handling facilities and Warehouse Receipt System of Area-based Agricultural Commodities in the Agriculture Sector in Uganda. - Strengthening governance for gender-responsive Climate Change planning and management in District Local Governments across all sectors. - Strengthening climate resilience of health care systems in climate change disaster risk prone areas in the Health and Disaster Risk Reduction.
Result for target 2.2: A capacity building workshop was organised for the national task force on carbon markets. Through the capacity building workshop, the understanding of the task force members was enhanced on the concepts of climate financing in the context of the Paris Agreement and the provisions and implications for Article 6 on cooperative and non-market approaches for climate financing, and the related provisions of the National Climate Change Act in the context of NDC implementation.
Result for target 2.3: A Designated Operating Entity called Carbon Check was involved to support the assessment of the draft Standardised baseline on improved cook stoves. 2 assessments have been conducted on the draft Standardised baseline. The final comments have been provided and the consultant is finalising the report based on the comments from the DOE. The SB provides enhance calculation of emission reductions in the cook stove sector.
Result for target 2.4: A Stakeholder engagement meeting organised with the Ministry of Water and Environment and the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development which discussed the draft Sstandardized baseline (SB)
Output 5: Sharing of best practices and knowledge management. Indicator 5: Number and type of knowledge products generated and disseminated (including gender targets Result against targets attained under output 3 indicator 3 Results for target 5.1: Africa Regional Monitoring Reporting and Verification (MRV) experience sharing dialogue was organised during the Africa Climate Week (ACW) The event was organised in collaboration with the UNFCCC Regional collaboration centre and the NDC Partnership. The Africa MRV side event was organised on 29th August 2022 as part of the Africa climate week. The event was attended by 80 participants from different countries. The event created a platform to share experiences among countries on MRV and the alignment of the MRV to article 6 reporting requirements under the Paris agreement.
